style.vernacular: Low coral-atoll town on a strip of land 20-400 m wide: one- and two-storey cement-block buildings, rendered or whitewashed and often left bare grey, under corrugated metal roofs in red, green or grey; a few traditional palm-thatch open-sided maneapa meeting houses; coral-gravel and sand ground, coconut palms and pandanus, with no high-rise.
style.ornament: Few applied ornaments: open-sided maneapa with steep thatch or tin roof on heavy posts, woven pandanus mat patterns, church blue-and-white paintwork, hand-painted signboards; buildings are plain and storm-hardened (Cyclone Bebe 1972 destroyed about 90% of houses).
